`continuable.rb` does the work: `checkpoint!` raises `Continuation::Interrupt` when the adapter reports `stopping?`, and `resume_job` then calls `retry_job` with `resume_options` (default `wait: 5.seconds`), while `serialize`/`deserialize` carry the continuation state and cursor into the next run. The other four supply the continuation state and cursor (`continuation.rb`, `continuation/step.rb`), the re-enqueue mechanism (`exceptions.rb`, where `retry_job` is defined), and the stopping signal (`abstract_adapter.rb`).
